physicalDetails.detail: Auburn braid, half undone over one shoulder by evening; grey under her eyes; shoulders held too square after being up since the night watch. Settles her quiver strap as she walks.

Stands at the cell threshold with her weight even on both feet, 'still as the frame', one hand near her quiver; braid brushes Jaina's shoulder when she turns sideways past the chair. Rides a horse; draws left-handed when needed.

Chapter 3: rides a gelding that throws its head at the spook; stands 'with her weight even' when reporting and when giving the count; hoods the lantern in a fold of her cloak to a slit; breaks a hazel switch off the bank and strips it with her thumbnail; kneels on the clay to count; unhooks her water skin for the child; turns her head after the carter's wagon and 'held it there a moment'.

Chapter 4: rides on Jaina's left; takes Sylvanas's bow when she dismounts; stands behind Sylvanas with a hand near her quiver; reports standing 'weight even'; walks along the granary wall with an arrow across the grip of her bow and lays a palm on the side-door planks; keeps the stair head with her bow; cuts Tam's sleeve from the arrow with her belt knife; goes round the girths at dawn without looking up; arrives in the night 'with the cold of the night on her cloak' carrying a cloth bundle.

Chapter 5: rides the left flank; watches the wood to the left 'at the height of a man' while the others laugh; takes Jaina's weight on her arm through a door and carries her to the gate; keeps her left hand by the quiver when reporting at the wall; lips move while counting; reads a ledger standing, one finger down the page.

Chapter 6 (seen from Jaina's POV): rides the left of the road in the old order; speaks only to the horses (leans down and talks into her horse's ear on the shy) and never aloud to a person on page. Draws the four horses in close at the camp and watches the soldiers' hands. Takes the mare's rein from Sylvanas at the hedge. Watches the empty army wagon's team's feet, 'the wide flat shoes heavy at the heel', until it is past. Her hand is near her quiver when the tally-man is stopped. Turns the horses for the road out of camp and takes the left of the road again on the afternoon traffic, watching ahead.

Chapter 7 (Sylvanas POV): on foot in the gate queue at Sylvanas's left shoulder, bow in hand; stands at the post window where she can see street and door; stands beside Sylvanas at the Fenner's lane corner, bow hand shifted on the stave; sits on the bench outside the post with her bow across her knees; takes the door at the table scene.

voiceMarkers.detail: Precise, orderly, field-report style: gives the sequence in order, volunteers observations (Kirin Tor ink dries violet at the edges, 'ours dries black'; staff matches the file wire and crystal).

Chapter 2: reports in a flat list ('Door was on the latch. Bowls on the table, a spoon in each...'), ends with a judgement ('I'd say they meant to come back to it'). With Jaina she is brief and practical ('Drink. Then mount from this side.', 'Slowly.'); does not joke and ignores Lyriel's gossip. Notes the cook-by-the-book facts: Jaina left the noon bowl, has eaten nothing since.

Chapter 3: reports the east-side sweep in a flat list ('East side's clear. Every house, the smithy, the inn's back rooms and loft. No one. No blood, no broken doors. Food on most tables, beds made in most, some shutters open... I'd say they went a few at a time.'); in the lane gives a tracker's inventory ('Feet. Boots. Clogs. Bare, here... This one drags the right toe') and refuses to guess a count ('I'd rather not give you a number and then take it back'); at the cut she is careful and skeptical ('It's a drove way... Half of this will be cattle... I can't tell you how much is people. I'd be guessing') and then gives a firm floor ('Sixty, Ranger-General. Sixty I'll put my name to... There'll be more.'); lowers and slows her voice as the count turns to alarm ('At least.').

Chapter 4: formal and exact, her voice 'level and carrying no farther than it needed to': 'Ranger-General. Shutters up on three houses, this side, since the bend. Middle of the day.' Reports the supply chain as a list with a number and no opinion ('Three months ago a new man came through with a cart, from the west road, offering barley and flour cheaper than the farms by two coppers on the measure. The keeper bought. He's bought four loads from him since, the last a fortnight ago... The keeper is pleased with the price.'). Understated field dry-ness in the night: 'Brask's man took my place on the stair. The woman at the end of Cooper's Lane was on her step watching the fire. I asked her for oats. She gave me these. Her own oats, from her own field. She wants the cloth back.'

Chapter 5: exact, numbered, dry reports: 'North road. Nine loads before the last month. Three since.', 'Thirty-one. In this book.', 'Forty-seven. Nineteen of them in more than one book.', 'fifty-three. Every one of them has Andorhal at one end.', 'Nine more with the end burned off.' Says 'Road's good' for 'the horses will do'. Offers one judgement when asked ('I'd say that was on purpose.', 'I'd say they were army wagons, going up full and coming back empty.'). At the ash she repeats 'Barov.' like a count and then stops. Corrects the count twice ('Cyndia counted twice').

Chapter 7: low, numbered reports led by 'Ranger-General.' ('Two in the arch with the spikes. One on the walk, and he hasn't looked out at the road since we joined the line. Two more inside by the trough, sitting down. Four of the five are watching the wagons.'; 'Eight that I'm sure of.'). Asks Havel one plain question at a time ('Where do they sleep, Captain?'; which end of the shed they unlock first). Gives the rope-walk report with a finger on Sylvanas's sketch, then takes it off.

beliefs.belief: Sylvanas's assumption that she expects only merchants and lost lordlings is contradicted by the arrest.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Sylvanas's belief about Cyndia, now contradicted.

beliefs.belief: The prisoner is a risk until proven otherwise: tracks her satchel, watches her reach for it.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Unresolved; she lets Jaina take out the book but 'Slowly'.

beliefs.belief: The villagers went 'a few at a time', not in a panic.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Fits Sylvanas's read of different hours; later contradicted in part by the girl's 'hundreds, all night, every night' and by the sixty-plus up the cow way, though both can be true if they rose over several nights.

beliefs.belief: A track count must be one she can put her name to, and she will not give one she may have to take back.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Held; she gives 'sixty' only after counting at the cut.

beliefs.belief: Chapter 7: a count must be exact and positional (who, where, what they do with their feet). Eight 'that I'm sure of'.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Borne out: Sylvanas reads the same eight as sentries.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Hold the roofs over the back lane by the chimney across from Kett's loft: watch windows, gables and the lane behind; no loose until Sylvanas calls.

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter6.active: Hold the left flank down the road to Andorhal's market gate; handle the horses, which shy and do not settle near the city; watch the traffic.

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter5.active: Hold the left flank on the south road into the hills; keep reading the road (wagon tracks, army shoes).

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter4.active: Cover the left flank on the ride south-west after the grain man; keep the loft safe; she has acted as Sylvanas's second pair of eyes and legs on supply this chapter.

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter3.active: Cover the left flank on the ride south with Sylvanas, Lyriel and the mage in the line.
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter3.underlying: Not shown on page; she has twice looked after the mage's hands and her mind, and her glance after the carter's wagon is an unspoken question.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Silent, exact, professional; no spoken reply to her roof assignment on the page (Lyriel says 'Mine.' for hers). No reaction to anything farewell-shaped (Ch9 hold stands).

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter6.state: Silent and watchful; no visible reaction on the page to the tally-man's farewell (Ch9 hold still applies). Works the shying horse with Sylvanas.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter5.state: Steady, focused and quiet; grew faster than Sylvanas at laying slips; silent about the Barov name after saying it twice; the only one not laughing in the wood: she was watching the trees. Sweeps the dark road alone and brings back the army-wagon finding.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter4.state: Even and dutiful; her only visible act of care is the bundle of oatcakes for Garran. Lyriel's glance at her in Brask's ledger line draws no reply. No sign shown of the carter's farewell on her mind.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter3.state: Controlled and wary, more careful with her voice after the count; the strange blessing caught her ear and she says nothing about it.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Sent a runner to Sylvanas with the prisoner's exact words; put the prisoner in the cell with the ward-stone and her gear under a damper; reinforced the guard; identified the prisoner as Jaina Proudmoore.
Pulled the wedge-shaped damper stone from the notch behind Jaina's chair when the party moved out; fetched the staff from the alcove; returned the satchel and pointed out the uneaten bowl.
Left the Pass post to ride south as shoulder escort to Sylvanas (the plan names her as active escort lead).

Scouted the abandoned farmhouse on foot and reported without entering; tracked the deer and wolf at the holly ('Nothing was chasing anything'); killed the surviving doe with a left-handed headshot; warned Jaina 'Slowly' at the satchel.
Swept the east side of Millhaven with Lyriel in a pair; covered the east road and the lane from the smithy corner during the well read; stood in the mill yard during the storehouse read.
Lit the way down the lane with a hooded lantern and read the churned prints in the dark; refused to give a count; said she lost the line at the gate at the top of the lane and 'didn't go through it'.

Stood in the hatch room doorway 'for some time' and gave her water skin to the child; wrapped the mage's hands on Sylvanas's order; gave Lyriel the girl's words 'in a low voice, all of them, in order' on the gallery.

Counted the drove way with two hazel switches laid a man's step apart while the mage called heavy and light, then reported sixty at least, four and five abreast, with every mark pointing uphill and a farm track gap passed by every one.
On the carter's approach brought her bow up on the left and kept it up after Sylvanas lowered her own, even after Lyriel lowered hers; turned her head after the wagon on the farewell.

Chapter 4: took Sylvanas's bow at the spear and rode behind her into the village; with Sylvanas interviewed the granary keeper (and, as reported, the keeper's sale history) and reported it to the chapel at dusk; watched the keeper drop the bar on the granary door; opened the unbarred side door; covered the loft stair and the boy; cut his sleeve free; stood at the loft stair so 'nobody comes up'; later got oatcake from Mother Haw for Garran and kept the stair till Brask's man relieved her.

Chapter 5: counted carts and chalk at Corley's gate; counted short-rate lines by road and date; sat with Corley while he copied the lines; discovered Hollow Green is in no book (the woman at the shop said they have their own mill); at the river depot checked yard, stables, wharf (raked yard, one horse and a trap, rope-marks on the crane posts) and reported 'on purpose'; on the Brill road crouched into a rut and found nothing heavy since the rain ('if six wagons came this way since the rain, they came by another road'); read the trap's tracks to the bridge; fetched the ash-pit bucket and sorted slips faster than Sylvanas; walked the south road to the first bridge at night and reported army wagons.

Chapter 6: took the left flank; held the mare's rein for Sylvanas at the hedge; drew the horses in close and watched the soldiers' hands at the camp; watched the empty army wagon's shoes; spoke to her shying horse and got it moving beside Sylvanas's; turned the party's horses out of the camp; went by the tally-man on the left without comment.

Chapter 7: counts the gate watchers; goes with Sylvanas and Havel into the district; holds Havel in the yard (asks him questions while Sylvanas tails the runner alone); counts the eight at Fenner's; watches the rope-walk and reports the three from the gate going up Hurdle Lane; is assigned the roofs across from Kett's loft.

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: Methodical documentation and observation (ink colour, staff match, file cross-check).
Tracking: reads track overlap (deer slots and wolf pads in the same track, wolf pads not spread for running).

Riding and archery under pressure: puts her horse across the road between the doe and Jaina's mare, draws left-handed, loses an arrow almost straight down into the skull ('a thud like a mallet on a tent peg').
Quiet observation: noted the frost a hand's width round Jaina's hand and that it went grey when lifted; reported it to Sylvanas.

Tracking in the dark: reads individual prints by hooded lantern ('bare... drags the right toe... a furrow in front of every print; he never lifted it'; 'Could be a foot. Could be something pulled along'); knows a drove way's seasonal use ('bring the beasts up here to the hill grazing in spring, and down again about now').

Counting method: lays two hazel switches across a cut a man's step apart to make a box and counts each marked print that falls inside it, then repeats the box up the cut; works with the mage's heavy-or-light marks.

Chapter 4: eyes for the village: spots three shuttered houses in the middle of the day before Jaina does; extracts a seller's timeline and prices from a granary keeper; notes the keeper dropped the bar from the outside (so the light in the loft means an intruder who came another way); a silent door-test on a leather hinge.

Chapter 5: ledger and paper work (counts, dates, cross-book duplicates, sorting burned slips by kind and order); rut-age reading on clay after rain; recognises shod-horse type (wide flat shoe, heavy heel: King's post horses she has seen at the Pass) and wheel load by depth; infers wagons full going up/empty coming down.
Chapter 6: reads army wagon teams by shoe at a glance (wide flat shoe, heavy at the heel), consistent with her Ch5 finding; handles a frightened Thalassian horse by voice at close quarters.

Chapter 7: gate watch-pattern count (five watchers, four on wagons, one on the wall not looking out); yard count of eight sentries with positions and posture; tracks the crew's movement at the bell (who locks in, who goes up the lane).

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Sylvanas (chapter 5)
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: 'Cyndia.' curt imperatives ('Cyndia. The yard and the gate.', 'Cyndia. Bring me everything in it. Use a bucket and don't shake it.').

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Lyriel (chapter 5)
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: Turns to her ('Lyriel turned to Cyndia') for audience; no name on page.

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Sylvanas
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: 'Cyndia' curt; no title ('Cyndia. Bring the lantern.', 'Wrap the mage's hands.'; chapter 4: 'Cyndia, with me.', 'Cyndia, tell her.', 'Cyndia, the stair. Nobody comes up.')

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Jaina (chapter 4)
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: Jaina still does not address her aloud; narration 'Cyndia' (by name).

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Jaina
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: Knows her only by the name someone in the passage called; does not address her aloud.

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Sylvanas (chapter 7)
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: 'Cyndia.' first name, curt orders by event ('Cyndia. The roofs over the back lane...'); 'my ranger' to Havel.

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Havel (chapter 7)
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: No name on page; answers her questions.

howSheAddressesOthers.pattern: 'Ranger-General' every time, including 'Ranger-General.' as a one-word acknowledgement (chapter 4 too).
No direct address on page; on the night round she reports to 'the room in general, as she would have reported to Sylvanas'.
No name, no title; imperatives only. Chapter 3: none on page; speaks of her only as 'the mage' through Sylvanas's mouth.
'Ranger-General' every time, low and at her shoulder; 'Captain' to Havel.

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Falls in at Sylvanas's shoulder; turns the file a quarter round to face her; stays in place at the cell threshold.

Weight even; off her horse before her name is finished; checks corners with an arrow on the string; reports at the stirrup; stands at the edge of the wood facing outward. Gives no sign of having heard Lyriel's joke.

Chapter 3: stands with weight even before reporting; stands with her back to a lane wall with an arrow on the string; lowers the lantern when told; hoods it in her cloak; goes down on her heels at the edge of a churn; lays her own finger near a print and not in it; walks up a cut with her lips moving; kneels a long while where the cut ends then comes back to halt in front of Sylvanas 'with her weight even on both feet'; keeps her bow up when others lower theirs; turns her head to follow the wagon and holds it there a moment.

Chapter 4: reports standing 'weight even'; keeps pace a step behind Sylvanas; takes the bow Sylvanas gives; stands at the stair head with an arrow on her string; lays her palm flat on a door to test it; cut a sleeve with a belt knife; reports to the room at large.

Chapter 6: stands 'at the left of the road' on rides; draws horses close and watches hands; leans down to speak into a horse's ear; follows the wagon's team's feet with her eyes. No glance, turn of the head, or reaction at the tally-man's farewell is shown on the page.

Chapter 7: speaks very low at Sylvanas's shoulder; shifts her bow hand on the stave when taking a task; lays her bow across her knees on the bench; takes the door post at the table; keeps still on the line (no spoken answer to the roof order on the page).

knowledge.detail: Knows the arrest sequence: crossed the outer ring before dawn unfelt; found at first light on the second ring at the split-cap stone below the high road; asked to stay, said the stones were sick from the inside; asked to be bound at the stone.
Has Jaina's staff, satchel and map; knows Kirin Tor ink and staff match the Farstrider file.
Knows the first farm was abandoned with the table laid, the child's coat on the peg, the cart gone south; knows the deer and wolf tracks in the holly.

Chapter 3: knows the east side of Millhaven is empty; the lane's prints (boots, clogs, bare feet, one dragging a toe, a longer drag); the girl's account (heard from Sylvanas's briefing and from the girl herself at the hatch); the drove way count (sixty at least, four and five abreast); the carter's exchange and farewell (she heard both).

Chapter 4: knows the granary keeper's supplier history (three months, four loads, west road, cheaper by two coppers on the measure) and that the bakehouse and most of the houses take from the granary; knows the keeper dropped the bar on the granary at supper and that the light in the loft therefore came from an intruder; knows Mother Haw's oats.

Chapter 5: knows the 31/47/53 counts, the short-rate dates, the swept depot, the shawl and trap tracks, the army wagon shoe (King's post horses at the Pass), and that the Barov seal is a shield with something on it. Has seen the King's post horses at the Pass.

Chapter 6: knows (as a listener) Jaina's plain line about the plague and the audience's outcome; the army wagons on the climb are the King's iron-tyred teams. Her Ch3 knowledge of the carter's farewell is NOT referenced or acted on on the page.

Chapter 7: knows the gate watchers, the eight at Fenner's, the rope-walk's two doors and which crew went where at the bell (the captain's men watched the crew in; the three from the gate went up Hurdle Lane). Hears Havel's account of the loaders. Her Ch3 carter knowledge is not touched.

arc.currentPosition: Chapter 4: still rigid and formal, effective: the left-hand escort and Sylvanas's investigator on the flour. Little interior shown (Jaina POV). Her Ch3 position follows.
arc.previousPosition_chapter3: Escort lead on the ride south and the independent witness to the carter's words (heard the grain-man question, Lyriel's answer and 'May the stars keep your road'); remains rigid, formal, watchful, careful about her numbers.
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter5: Chapter 5: Sylvanas's second pair of hands on paper and ground; trusted to count and sort, and does it faster than Sylvanas by the end; still rigid, formal, minimal, does not laugh.
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter6: Chapter 6: background escort. Silent, left flank, horses and soldiers' hands. No reaction held for the farewell (Ch9).
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter7: Chapter 7: Sylvanas's counter and Havel-minder; her counts make the picture of the yard. Left alone with Havel while Sylvanas tails the runner; gets the roofs for the capture.
